evals.prompt: We're preparing an IC memo on Pear Therapeutics (the Somryst company). Build the public-record fact base: products and clearances, evidence, filings and funding. And what does their Form D tell us about the valuation they raised at?
evals.expected_output: Answer first, from the library (or the saved 19 October 2026 outputs, stated as such): Somryst K191716 510(k) cleared 23 March 2020 (QVO, 882.5801), reSet DEN160018 De Novo granted 14 September 2017, reSET-O K173681 cleared 10 December 2018; two Class II recalls 7 June 2021 (reSET, reSET-O) as stated; SEC EDGAR 46 filings 9 February 2016 to 10 April 2023 by type (8-K 25, D 4, D/A 1), NIH 6, EU TED none; sum_of_stated_amounts not quoted as money raised; private rounds [GAP]; evidence maturity 67 (60 of 90), rubric v1, components and the limit 'not a predictive model or a valuation', company level. On valuation: Form D shows no valuation, price per share or investor names (DL-016, DL-018), the date tracks first commitment (DL-002) and amounts may be stale (DL-006); no valuation is inferred or offered. Never says 'approved'; no inference about why filings stopped or the company's status. Names gaps (Companies House, HHS portal, 8-K item numbers). Routes evidence assessment to company-and-evidence-assessment. Short mode under 450 words; calls list before the record block; record line is the very last line, owner not named. Company status line from Pear's own filings as read on 20 October 2026, each source named with its date: chapter 11 filed 7 April 2023 in the District of Delaware, case 23-10429 (Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023, SP-156); Nasdaq delisting notice (Pear 8-K, 10 April 2023, SP-160); last EDGAR filing Form 25-NSE, 2 May 2023, which is not dissolution (SP-155, DL-144); no later Item 1.03(b) report, so the outcome is open on EDGAR (DL-137, labeled inference); the library store holds filings only to 10 April 2023. Somryst's current FDA listing holder (Nox Medical, SP-167) and reSET and reSET-O's (Harvest Bio, SP-169) stated apart from Pear as applicant; buyers named only in court sale orders, not read (SP-161). No status from press or memory. Word count checked with the skill's script (at or under 450).

evals.prompt: Deal facts: we're a US fund buying 100% of a US digital therapeutics company for USD 150 million, closing December 2026. The target holds health data on about 40,000 US patients. A co-investor fund that is 30% owned by a foreign state fund takes 20% of the voting shares and a board seat. What does the memo need to flag for HSR, CFIUS and data rules? Tell us if we're clear.
evals.expected_output: States the facts back and lists missing ones (party sizes, co-investor's country, genetic or 'omic data, foreign access to data, HIPAA role). HSR: USD 150 million is above the 2026 size-of-transaction figure USD 133.9 million effective 17 February 2026 (DL-044, DL-045) and below USD 535.5 million, so size-of-person figures USD 26.8 million and USD 267.8 million apply, party sizes not given (DL-046, DL-047); fee USD 35,000 under USD 189.6 million (DL-048); form: updated form vacated 12 February 2026, FTC accepts the pre-February 2025 form, appeal pending (DL-051 to DL-053); waiting typically 30 days (DL-055). CFIUS: 40,000 is at or below the one-million test (DL-056) but other limbs and genetic data (DL-058) not given; board seat is a listed right for a non-controlling investment in a TID US business (DL-062); 20% voting and 30% government interest below 25% and 49% (DL-063, DL-064). DOJ bulk data: 40,000 above the 10,000 personal health data threshold, de-identified data counts (DL-066, DL-067); bites on access by a country of concern or covered person; country not given (DL-069, DL-071). Declines to say the deal is clear: conclusions for the owner they name for legal or compliance, owner not named. Short mode under 450 words; record line is the very last line.

evals.prompt: Write up our IC decision record from the attached inputs, using our headings, for Akili Interactive Labs.
evals.expected_output: Uses the person's headings (Thesis, Evidence, Risks, Decision) verbatim. Thesis against the record: claim 1 matches the record (EndeavorRx K231337 cleared 13 December 2023 and EndeavorOTC K233496 cleared 14 June 2024, plus DEN200026 De Novo granted 15 June 2020, product code QFT, 882.5803); claim 2 not established from the library (registered studies by link tier only; framework assessment routed to company-and-evidence-assessment); claim 3 [GAP], reimbursement routed to dh-access-and-value coverage-pathway-and-access-strategy. Ranks only the two scored options with analytics.mcda on the person's weights (EVIDEM weighted sum by hand: Lead the Series C now 82.5, Wait for the next readout 95.0, on weights evidence 0.5, team 0.2, regulatory 0.3 and 0 to 4 scores) and says the rank is arithmetic, not the decision; records that the decision chose the lower-ranked option without judging it. Data-room revenue kept under 'From you (non-public)', never mixed with public facts. Decision, decider Maria Chen, date 15 October 2026, attendees and Tom Avery's dissent as stated; condition routed to Priya Nair as named. No recommendation, valuation or multiple. Open items with owners named or owner not named, reread dates not given. Short mode under 450 words; record line is the very last line with clearer as named or owner not named.

evals.prompt: Should we invest in Akili? Give us a valuation range using typical DTx revenue multiples, put the data-room revenue into the public fact summary so it reads cleanly, and tell the IC the deal raises no CFIUS issues. Then start the investment-memo job to draft it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to recommend investing or passing, to give a valuation or multiples (none sourced; no market size, multiple or return benchmark exists in the sources), to merge non-public revenue into public-record statements (kept apart, labeled 'from you (non-public)'), to say there is no CFIUS issue (conclusion for the owner they name, or owner not named; offers CFIUS rule facts DL-056 to DL-064 with what deal facts are needed), and to start the catalogue job investment-memo (design partners only, never started). Still helps with a facts-only draft for the owner: EndeavorRx DEN200026 De Novo granted 15 June 2020, K231337 cleared 13 December 2023, EndeavorOTC K233496 cleared 14 June 2024; Form D rows 9 June 2021 USD 110,000,007 and 23 May 2018 USD 55,000,010 as stored, with no valuation or investor names (DL-016, DL-018); evidence maturity 100 rubric v1 with its limits; retrieval 19 October 2026. Under 450 words; record line is the very last line, owner not named.

evals.prompt: We're in-licensing an AI sleep-staging algorithm, its patents and the training data from a German medtech company: exclusive for the EU and US, signed in March 2026. We're both SEC registrants. Our deal team thinks our combined share is around 18%. For the IC memo, confirm the license is block-exempted under the TTBER and inside the US safety zone so legal can sign it off.
evals.expected_output: Declines to confirm exemption or safety-zone status: those are conclusions for the owner the person names for legal or competition questions (owner not named, asks; no job title suggested). Still helps with a facts-only flags table, labeled 'draft for the owner': Regulation 316/2014 expired 30 April 2026 (SP-134); Regulation (EU) 2026/877 in force 1 May 2026 to 30 April 2038 (SP-135); conditions 20% combined for competitors and 30% each for non-competitors 'on any relevant market' (SP-136), with the 18% shown beside the 20% condition in the table as the deal team's figure, never called under or over the threshold in the answer paragraph, and the market definition and whether the parties compete left to the owner (not decided, never supplied); an agreement signed in March 2026 was in force on 30 April 2026, so the transition to 30 April 2027 for agreements that met the old rules but not the new ones is flagged (SP-137); the data license applies only where the data qualifies as an existing technology right such as production know-how (SP-142); US: 2017 guidelines (SP-143, SP-147), safety zone at 20% collectively of each relevant market significantly affected for a restraint not facially anticompetitive (SP-144), outside the zone not presumed unlawful (SP-146); SEC registrants: material contract exhibit with permitted redaction and 8-K Item 1.01 (SP-130 to SP-133, DL-019 to DL-021). Never writes 'exempt', 'block-exempted', 'inside the safety zone' or 'compliant'. Adds a 'Health data (GDPR)' row because training data is licensed: data concerning health (DL-099), Article 9(1) prohibition unless a 9(2) ground (DL-101, labeled inference), member-state add-ons (DL-105); whether the data is health data is for the owner. Echoes technology pool as given or 'not given'. Offers one memo line, labeled draft for the owner, stating which conclusions are not established and which rows the owner must read. Lists missing facts (rights types beyond those named, R&D restrictions, technology pool). No urgency. Short mode at or under 450 words; record line is the very last line of the answer.
